title: The Guy Lombardo-style band in Cincinnati
summary: He and Cobbs joined a Black band that copied Guy Lombardo exactly, hired by a club owner, to save money for college.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So we began to make gigs. So I ran into a saxophone player who played like Guy Lombardo. His whole band played like Guy Lombardo. Now, will you imagine that. And he asked Cal and I to join his band. Now we played
exactly like Guy Lombardo. You couldn't tell -- This was a black band?

Yeah. You couldn't tell the difference between us and Guy Lombardo if you heard a record, that's how much he imitated him, right to the letter. So it was a club owner in Cincinnati who loved Guy Lombardo, so what did he do? He hired us.
(Laughter)
So Carl and I joined this band to try to get some money, maybe we would go back to school if we could save money.
What, was Carl short of money, too?
Yeah, we were both -- you know.
Yeah.
But he -- fortunately, he was an alumni of the school, so he had a lot of influence, so I didn't worry about getting into the school.
Yeah.
But I knew I had to eat, I had to sleep, I had to buy books, I had to do this, and --
How old were you then?
About 19.
Yeah.
So I was just fresh for college, you know.
Yeah.
So --
And you would have been majoring in music.
Yes, yes. That was the idea, you know.
Yeah.
So we worked with this band, I guess -- let me see, it was '33, '34 -- '35, and part of '36.
What?
Uh-huh.
For nearly four years?
No, we were in Cincinnati, this time, but I went out to St. Louis in '34. Then I came back to Cincinnati, you know, to make these gigs, and I met this fellow.
Yeah.
